scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service subscription canceled 34 days ago, which is slightly outside the standard 30-day refund policy window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Jamal Washington and I'm 38. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Jamal. I understand you're looking for a refund on a subscription charge that occurred after your cancellation. I’d be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the last four digits of the payment method used?
Sure, the email is j.washington@email.com and the card ends in 4492.
Thank you, Jamal. I have located your account. For security, could you please confirm your billing zip code?

Verification complete, thank you. I see the cancellation was processed on the 34th day prior to today. While our 'Service Refund Policy 4.2' typically mandates a 30-day window for full refunds, I can see you have been a loyal member with us for three years. I am authorized to grant a one-time exception for accounts in good standing.
That would be a huge help, thank you so much for understanding.

You're very welcome. I have successfully processed the refund of $49.99 to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit reflect on your statement within 3-5 business days depending on your bank. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
No, that covers everything. Thanks again for the quick help!

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account, acknowledged the policy exception, and processed a full refund as a one-time courtesy for a loyal customer.

judge_scores.justification: The agent conducted appropriate security verification, maintained a warm and empathetic tone while addressing the customer's specific situation, and efficiently processed the refund. Furthermore, the agent correctly cited specific policy 4.2 and used their authority to grant a warranted one-time exception for a loyal customer without requiring an unnecessary escalation.
